beats.text: It was not simply pounds against kilograms.
beats.note: The Board of Inquiry called that explanation simplistic and inaccurate. The crew used a factor of 1.77, which converts litres to pounds, where one for kilograms, about 0.8, was needed.

beats.name: Air Canada Flight 143
beats.role: A Boeing 767 needed 22,300 kilograms of fuel. It left with roughly 10,000 kilograms, less than half, and nobody on board knew.

beats.note: About 65 miles from Winnipeg and 45 miles from Gimli, a former air force base, according to the Board of Inquiry.

beats.name: Robert Pearson
beats.role: The captain. First Officer Maurice Quintal had once been stationed at Gimli himself, and the pair glided the 767 towards the old base.

beats.context: Aboard: 61 passengers and 8 crew. Everyone lived. The jet touched down within 800 feet of the threshold of a 7,200 foot runway.
